Impact craters and basins by diameter.Meteor Crater (Arizona): Around 50,000 years ago an iron meteorite blasted this hole in the desert. Apollo astronauts trained here before heading to the Moon.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Tycho (Moon): This young Moon crater, only about 100 million years old, is surrounded by bright rays of ejecta that stretch for over a thousand kilometers.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Herschel (Mimas): Herschel gives tiny Mimas, a moon of Saturn, a strong resemblance to the Death Star. The impact almost shattered the moon.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Chicxulub (Earth): This crater under the Yucatán is linked to the dinosaurs' extinction 66 million years ago. Oil prospectors first noticed it by its gravity.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Vredefort (Earth): South Africa's Vredefort Dome is the largest verified impact structure on Earth. It is about two billion years old and a World Heritage site.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Rheasilvia (Vesta): Its central peak rises about 20 km, over twice the height of Everest. NASA's Dawn spacecraft mapped it from orbit.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Mare Imbrium (Moon): The 'Sea of Showers' formed from an impact some 3.9 billion years ago and was later flooded with dark lava. Apollo 15 landed at its edge.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Caloris (Mercury): Named Caloris, Latin for heat, because it lies where the Sun is overhead at Mercury's hottest times. Its impact may have scrambled the opposite side.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.Hellas (Mars): The deepest region of Mars, around 7 km deep, so air pressure there is high enough for frost to sometimes form.
Impact craters and basins by diameter.South Pole-Aitken (Moon): On the Moon's far side, this is the largest, oldest and deepest known crater in the Solar System. China's Chang'e 6 brought back samples in 2024.

Solar System worlds by diameter.Pluto: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, and its diameter is less than the width of the United States.
Solar System worlds by diameter.The Moon: The Moon is about a quarter of Earth's diameter, and its gravitational pull creates the ocean tides.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Mercury: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System, and it has a huge iron core and extreme temperature swings.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Mars: Mars is about half the diameter of Earth, and it has Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Venus: Venus is almost the same size as Earth, but its thick atmosphere traps heat, making it the hottest planet.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Earth: Earth is the largest of the rocky planets, and it is the only world known to harbour life.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Neptune: Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun, and its winds are the fastest in the Solar System.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Uranus: Uranus rotates on its side, likely the result of an ancient collision, so its poles take turns facing the Sun.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Saturn: Saturn's rings are mostly water ice, and the planet is so light that it would float in a big enough bathtub.
Solar System worlds by diameter.Jupiter: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined, and its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.

Debut album years of these pop stars.Madonna: Her self-titled debut brought 'Holiday' and 'Lucky Star' and began her rise to best-selling female recording artist ever.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Whitney Houston: Her debut became one of the best-selling debut albums ever and produced three US number-one singles, including 'Saving All My Love for You'.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Mariah Carey: Her self-titled debut produced four straight US number-one singles, starting with 'Vision of Love', and won her the Best New Artist Grammy.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Britney Spears: Her debut '...Baby One More Time' topped the Billboard 200, and its title single came with a famous schoolgirl-uniform video.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Beyoncé (solo): Dangerously in Love came after Destiny's Child, was powered by 'Crazy in Love', and won her five Grammys in one night.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Rihanna: Music of the Sun arrived when she was 17, fresh from Barbados, after producer Evan Rogers discovered her.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Lady Gaga: The Fame brought 'Just Dance' and 'Poker Face'. She had honed the act in New York's Lower East Side clubs before the deal.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Ariana Grande: Yours Truly entered the Billboard 200 at number one. She was already known as Cat Valentine on Nickelodeon's Victorious.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Dua Lipa: Her self-titled debut included 'New Rules'. She was born in London to Kosovo-Albanian parents and began posting covers online as a teen.
Debut album years of these pop stars.Olivia Rodrigo: SOUR followed her smash 'drivers license', released when she was 18. She had been a Disney Channel actress before topping charts.

How many holes?.Bagel: Traditionally boiled before baking, which gives it a chewy crust, and the hole helps it cook evenly.
How many holes?.Your nose: Your nasal cycle quietly switches which nostril does most of the breathing every few hours.
How many holes?.Bowling ball: Balls are drilled to fit the bowler's grip, and the holes are placed off-centre on purpose.
How many holes?.Tin whistle: Also called the penny whistle, a cheap staple of Irish folk music that anybody can pick up.
How many holes?.Ritz cracker: Bakers call them docking holes: they let steam escape so the cracker bakes flat instead of puffing up.
How many holes?.Recorder: Henry VIII reportedly owned dozens of recorders, and the instrument fell from fashion after the flute rose.
How many holes?.Standard harmonica: Each of the ten holes gives a different note when you blow or draw, producing up to 19 notes.
How many holes?.Saltine cracker: Called soda crackers for the baking soda used, its holes keep the dough from blistering as it bakes.
How many holes?.Battleship target grid: The game began as a pencil-and-paper game before the plastic peg version, and hits are marked with red pegs.
How many holes?.Chinese checkers board: It's not Chinese: it derives from the German game Stern-Halma, renamed in the 1920s by US marketers.

Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Na (sodium): From Latin natrium, from natron, a natural salt, and it's also why sodium is related to 'soda'.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.K (potassium): From Latin kalium, from Arabic 'al-qalyah', meaning the ashes of plants, the source of potash.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Fe (iron): From Latin ferrum, it's the most common element by mass on Earth, mostly locked in the core.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Ag (silver): From Latin argentum, which is also how Argentina got its name, the land of silver.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Sn (tin): From Latin stannum. Mixed with copper, tin makes bronze, which started the Bronze Age.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Sb (antimony): From Latin stibium. Its ore stibnite was ground into kohl and used as eyeliner in ancient Egypt.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.W (tungsten): The W comes from German 'wolfram', and it has the highest melting point of any metal, about 3,400 °C.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Au (gold): From Latin aurum. All the gold ever mined would fit in roughly four Olympic swimming pools.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Hg (mercury): From Latin hydrargyrum, 'water-silver', which is why it was also called quicksilver.
Odd element symbols, by atomic number.Pb (lead): From Latin plumbum, which is also the root of 'plumber', because Romans piped water through lead.

Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Boy Jesus in the Temple: Only Luke tells this one: at twelve, Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem and his parents found him after three days, talking with teachers.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Baptism by John: In the Jordan River, the Gospels describe a voice from heaven and a dove descending, marking the start of his public ministry.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Temptation in the wilderness: Jesus fasted forty days in the desert, and the tempter's offers included turning stones into bread.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Feeding of the 5,000: The only miracle of Jesus recorded in all four Gospels, performed with five loaves and two fish.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Transfiguration: On a mountain Jesus's face shone and Moses and Elijah appeared; only Peter, James and John witnessed it.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Raising of Lazarus: Told only in John: Lazarus had been in the tomb four days, and the famous short verse 'Jesus wept' comes from this story.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Empty tomb: All four Gospels name Mary Magdalene among the women who first found it empty on Sunday morning.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Road to Emmaus: Two followers walk with a stranger they only recognise when he breaks bread; Luke names one of them as Cleopas.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Ascension: Luke narrates this twice, at the end of his Gospel and the start of Acts, where it comes forty days after Easter.
Gospel and Acts events, in story order.Pentecost: Acts says the disciples spoke in other languages; it coincided with the Jewish harvest festival of Shavuot, fifty days after Passover.

How high off the ground.Table tennis net: Standard table tennis nets are only about 15 cm tall, which is why players can slice the ball so low across them that it barely clears.
How high off the ground.Cricket stumps: Cricket stumps stand 28 inches tall, and the bails resting on top are sometimes knocked off by a ball hit with enough force to dislodge them.
How high off the ground.Tennis net (centre): The tennis net is held at 3 ft 6 in at the posts, but sags lower in the middle, which is why the centre strap is set to exactly 3 ft.
How high off the ground.Men's sprint hurdle: Hurdlers in men's 110 m sprints clear ten of these barriers, and they are built to tip over so a clip does not cause a nasty fall.
How high off the ground.Ice hockey goal: The NHL goal measures 6 feet wide by 4 feet high, so a goalie must cover the huge space with pads, blocker and trapper.
How high off the ground.Badminton net (centre): Badminton nets are set at 5 ft 1 in in the centre and slightly higher at the posts, a small difference that matters for smashes.
How high off the ground.Soccer crossbar: The soccer crossbar stands 8 feet from the ground, a height unchanged since the 19th-century rules that said it must be fixed that way.
How high off the ground.Basketball rim: Basketball's 10-foot rim was set by the inventor, James Naismith, who nailed peach baskets to a gym balcony that happened to be that high.
How high off the ground.Olympic diving platform: Olympic diving platforms reach 10 m, and divers hit the water at about 50 km/h, so the pool is carefully aerated to soften the splash.
How high off the ground.Men's high diving platform: Cliff and high diving from 27 m means entering the water near 85 km/h, and divers have only about three seconds to complete their somersaults.

How well these kitchen materials conduct.Air: Air is a poor conductor, which is why it is trapped in insulation, double glazing and down jackets to keep heat in.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Wooden spoon: Wood is an excellent heat insulator, so wooden spoons stay comfortable to hold while the pot of soup in front of them is boiling.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Teflon coating: Teflon is the brand name of a fluoropolymer, PTFE, which was discovered by accident in 1938 while chemists were studying refrigerants.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Water: Water conducts heat far better than air, which is why a bath at the same temperature as the air feels cold much more quickly.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Pyrex glass: Pyrex was developed by Corning, and the original borosilicate formula was designed to resist the thermal shock that cracks regular glass.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Stainless steel: Stainless steel is a poor conductor for a metal, so quality pans often sandwich an aluminium or copper core inside the steel.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Cast iron: Cast iron heats slowly and unevenly but holds heat for ages, which is why a skillet is so good at searing steaks.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Aluminum: Aluminum conducts heat remarkably well and is light, which is why it is the most common material for baking trays and many saucepans.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Copper: Copper pans are favored by professional cooks because they react to heat changes almost instantly, giving very fine control.
How well these kitchen materials conduct.Silver: Silver beats every other metal at conducting heat, though it is far too costly and soft for most cookware.

When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Krispy Kreme: Krispy Kreme began in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and its glowing Hot Now sign signals fresh doughnuts.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Winchell's Donuts: Winchell's Donuts began in California, and it was a pioneer of the doughnut shop in the US West.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Dunkin': Dunkin' was founded by William Rosenberg in Massachusetts, and it was originally called Dunkin' Donuts.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Tim Hortons: Tim Hortons was founded by a hockey star, and it has become a Canadian cultural icon.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Mrs. Fields: Mrs. Fields began with Debbi Fields selling cookies in Palo Alto, and she became a baking sensation.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Cinnabon: Cinnabon was founded in Seattle, and its secret was a special cinnamon sold under the name Makara.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Auntie Anne's: Auntie Anne's started as a stand at a farmers' market in Pennsylvania, and its founder used it to fund a counselling ministry.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Wetzel's Pretzels: Wetzel's Pretzels began in a Southern California mall, and it popularized fresh-baked pretzels in malls.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Insomnia Cookies: Insomnia Cookies began in a college dorm room, and it delivers warm cookies late at night.
When these doughnut, cookie and pretzel.Duck Donuts: Duck Donuts is known for making doughnuts to order, and it began in Duck, North Carolina, a beach town.

Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.Tin Man (Oz): L. Frank Baum's woodman debuted in the 1900 novel. In the 1939 film, aluminum makeup sent the original actor, Buddy Ebsen, to the hospital.
Karel Capek's play gave the world the word 'robot', from the Czech 'robota' meaning forced labor, and its robots were more like bioengineered workers.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.Maria (Metropolis): Fritz Lang's silent film gave us a gleaming female robot built to impersonate a human, a design that influenced C-3PO decades later.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.Robby the Robot: He appeared in Forbidden Planet, and the suit was so loved that MGM reused it in many productions, including TV shows, for years afterward.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.The Daleks: Their first appearance on Doctor Who in 1963 turned a low-budget serial into a hit, and they are really cyborg creatures inside the casings.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.HAL 9000: Its name was said to come from 'Heuristic ALgorithmic'. The popular idea that the letters sit one step before IBM is a myth the creators denied.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.R2-D2: Ben Burtt created this droid's beeps and whistles by blending electronic synth sounds with his own voice, with no actual words.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.The Terminator: James Cameron has said the idea came from a fever dream of a metal skeleton rising from flames, and the title cyborg has remarkably little dialogue.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.Data (Star Trek): The android in Star Trek: The Next Generation, who longs to be human, can't use contractions and has a pale, golden complexion.
Robots and AIs of fiction, by debut.WALL-E: Pixar's trash-compacting robot barely speaks in the film's first act, with sound designer Ben Burtt also creating its voice and blips.

When these services shut down.GeoCities (US): GeoCities let millions of people build free home pages, and its closure erased a huge part of early web culture.
When these services shut down.MSN Messenger: MSN Messenger, with its nudge and winks, was once the way teens chatted, and it was replaced by Skype.
When these services shut down.Orkut: Orkut, made by a Google engineer of the same name, was a social network that became hugely popular in Brazil and India.
When these services shut down.Vine: Vine limited videos to six seconds and launched many careers, and it was bought by Twitter before being shut down.
When these services shut down.Google+ (consumer): Google+ was Google's attempt to take on Facebook, and a data bug exposed users' private information, hastening its end.
When these services shut down.Adobe Flash: Adobe Flash powered the web's games and animations for many years, but its end came after smartphones refused to support it.
When these services shut down.Yahoo Answers: Yahoo Answers was a question-and-answer site whose strange questions became the stuff of internet memes.
When these services shut down.Internet Explorer: Internet Explorer was once used by more than 90 percent of web users, and its successor was Microsoft Edge.
When these services shut down.Google Stadia: Google Stadia was a game-streaming service that failed to catch on, and Google refunded many purchases.
When these services shut down.Skype: Skype popularized free video calls over the internet, and was bought by Microsoft for 8.5 billion dollars in 2011.

The life of the Buddha, in story order.Born in Lumbini: The Buddha was born in Lumbini, in present-day Nepal, a site marked by an inscribed pillar placed by Emperor Ashoka.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.Asita's prophecy: The sage Asita is said to have predicted that the baby prince would become either a great ruler or a great spiritual teacher.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.Marries Yasodhara: Siddhartha married Yasodhara, and had a son named Rahula, whose name means 'fetter'.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.The Four Sights: The Four Sights, an old man, a sick man, a corpse and a wandering ascetic, made the prince see suffering for the first time.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.The Great Renunciation: The Great Renunciation is when Siddhartha left his palace at night, cut his hair and began the life of a wandering seeker.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.Years of harsh asceticism: The Buddha tried extreme fasting for six years, and later taught the Middle Way between luxury and self-denial.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.Sujata's bowl of milk-rice: Sujata, a village woman, offered milk-rice to the starving ascetic, and it restored his strength before enlightenment.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.Enlightenment: He sat under a bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, and the site is among the holiest in Buddhism, with a descendant of the tree still there.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.First sermon at Sarnath: The Buddha gave his first teaching at Sarnath, near Varanasi, to five former companions, and set the 'wheel of dharma' in motion.
The life of the Buddha, in story order.Parinirvana: Parinirvana is the Buddha's final passing, at Kushinagar, where he is depicted lying on his side in many statues.

When the Sun enters these constellations.Aquarius: The Sun's real position differs from astrological sign dates because Earth's axis has shifted since ancient times.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Pisces: Two fish tied by a cord. The March equinox point currently lies in Pisces, but it is drifting toward Aquarius.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Aries: The equinox point was in Aries about 2,000 years ago, and astronomers still call it the First Point of Aries.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Taurus: It holds the Pleiades and the Hyades star clusters, plus the Crab Nebula, remnant of a supernova seen in 1054.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Gemini: Named for the twins Castor and Pollux. The Geminid meteor shower each December is one of the year's best.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Cancer: Among the faintest zodiac constellations, yet it holds the Beehive Cluster, a fuzzy patch visible to the naked eye in dark skies.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Leo: Its bright star Regulus marks the lion's heart, and the Leonid meteor shower seems to radiate from here each November.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Virgo: The second-largest constellation, home to the Virgo Cluster, a collection of well over a thousand galaxies.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Scorpius: Antares, the red supergiant at its heart, means "rival of Mars". The Sun passes through this constellation in barely a week.
When the Sun enters these constellations.Ophiuchus: The serpent-bearer is the "thirteenth zodiac constellation": the Sun crosses it for about two weeks, but astrology ignores it.

Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Mont Blanc Tunnel: Opened in 1965 between France and Italy beneath the Alps; a fire in 1999 killed 39 people and closed it for three years.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Fréjus Road Tunnel: The road tunnel opened in 1980 beside an older rail tunnel through the same mountain, which dates from 1871 and was one of the great Alpine engineering feats.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Gotthard Road Tunnel: Opened in 1980, it was the world's longest road tunnel for twenty years, and it is a single bore carrying traffic both ways.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Simplon Tunnel: Two single-track rail tubes opened in 1906; it was the world's longest railway tunnel for over 70 years, linking Switzerland and Italy.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Lærdal Tunnel, Norway: The world's longest road tunnel; designers added three caverns lit in blue and yellow, like a sunrise, to break the monotony for drivers.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Guadarrama Tunnel, Spain: Spain's high-speed trains between Madrid and Valladolid rush through this twin-bore tunnel beneath the Sierra de Guadarrama, which opened in 2007.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Lötschberg Base Tunnel: This Swiss rail tunnel under the Bernese Alps opened in 2007 and lets trains run up to 250 km/h, cutting the trip between Bern and Brig.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Channel Tunnel: It has three tubes, two for trains and a central service tunnel, and about 38 km of it is under the sea, the longest undersea section of any tunnel.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Seikan Tunnel, Japan: It links Honshu to Hokkaido and plunges about 240 meters below sea level at its deepest; Shinkansen bullet trains have used it since 2016.
Lengths of the world's great tunnels.Gotthard Base Tunnel: The world's longest and deepest railway tunnel opened in 2016, with up to about 2,300 meters of rock overhead.

When these trailblazing women made histo.Seneca Falls Convention: The first US women's rights convention, held in upstate New York; its Declaration of Sentiments echoed the Declaration of Independence.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Nellie Bly's world trip: Journalist Elizabeth Cochran, writing as Nellie Bly, circled the globe in 72 days, beating the fictional Phileas Fogg's 80.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Marie Curie's first Nobel: Marie shared the 1903 Physics Prize with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel and later won again in Chemistry in 1911.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Nancy Astor takes Commons seat: She was the first woman to sit in the UK House of Commons; Constance Markievicz was elected first but refused to take her seat.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Earhart flies Atlantic solo: She flew from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland in around 15 hours, earning the Distinguished Flying Cross.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Rosa Parks stays seated: Her refusal on a Montgomery bus sparked a 381-day boycott, and the Supreme Court later struck down segregated buses.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Tereshkova goes to space: A cotton-mill worker and amateur skydiver, she orbited Earth 48 times aboard Vostok 6.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Junko Tabei climbs Everest: The first woman to summit Everest, she survived an avalanche that buried her days before the climb.
When these trailblazing women made histo.O'Connor joins Supreme Court: Sandra Day O'Connor, appointed by Ronald Reagan, was the first woman on the US Supreme Court and served until 2006.
When these trailblazing women made histo.Sally Ride goes to space: She flew on Challenger as the first American woman in space, and at 32 was then the youngest American astronaut.

Great physicists, by birth year.Christiaan Huygens: He discovered Saturn's moon Titan, explained its rings as a disc, and built the first pendulum clock.
Great physicists, by birth year.Michael Faraday: Largely self-taught, he found electromagnetic induction, which underlies electric generators, and gave Christmas lectures that still run today.
Great physicists, by birth year.James Clerk Maxwell: His four equations united electricity, magnetism and light; Einstein kept his portrait on the wall of his study.
Great physicists, by birth year.Max Planck: He launched quantum theory in 1900 by proposing that energy comes in discrete packets, and a constant bears his name.
Great physicists, by birth year.Ernest Rutherford: Born in New Zealand, he showed the atom has a tiny dense nucleus and first split the atom in 1917.
Great physicists, by birth year.Niels Bohr: His 1913 atomic model put electrons in fixed orbits, and the element bohrium is named after him.
Great physicists, by birth year.Erwin Schrödinger: His wave equation underpins quantum mechanics, and his famous cat thought experiment mocked a puzzle in its interpretation.
Great physicists, by birth year.Werner Heisenberg: His uncertainty principle says certain pairs, like a particle's position and momentum, can't both be known precisely.
Great physicists, by birth year.J. Robert Oppenheimer: He directed the Los Alamos laboratory that built the first atomic bombs, tested at Trinity in July 1945.
Great physicists, by birth year.Richard Feynman: Famous for his diagrams of particle interactions, he also dunked an O-ring in ice water to explain the Challenger disaster.

When did these first appear on Earth?.First fish: Early jawless fish like Haikouichthys swam in Cambrian seas; true jaws came many millions of years later.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First four-legged animals: Fossils like Tiktaalik show fins turning into limbs with wrist-like joints, a key step toward life on land.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First reptiles: Reptiles laid shelled eggs that did not dry out, freeing them from having to breed in water the way amphibians do.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First mammals: The first mammals were tiny, probably nocturnal creatures that lived in the shadow of the dinosaurs.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First birds: Archaeopteryx, found in German limestone, had feathers and wings but also teeth and a bony tail, like a dinosaur.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First primates: Early primates were small tree-dwellers; grasping hands and forward-facing eyes helped them judge branches.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First whales (Pakicetus): This wolf-sized, land-dwelling animal from Pakistan is an ancestor of whales, which evolved from hoofed mammals.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First apes: Apes are distinguished from monkeys mostly by having no tail; today's apes include gibbons, orangutans and us.
When did these first appear on Earth?.First hominins: A skull from Chad nicknamed Toumai may belong to one of the earliest members of the human family tree.
When did these first appear on Earth?.Homo sapiens: The oldest known fossils of our species, from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, are about 300,000 years old; a tiny slice of Earth's history.

The 1910s, one event per year.Japan annexes Korea: Japan ruled Korea until 1945, when the end of World War II finally freed the peninsula from its control.
The 1910s, one event per year.Xinhai Revolution: The revolution ended the Qing dynasty and the 2,000-year imperial tradition, and led to the Republic of China.
The 1910s, one event per year.Titanic sinks: It sank after hitting an iceberg on its maiden voyage, with lifeboats for only about half of those aboard.
The 1910s, one event per year.US Federal Reserve created: The act created a central bank for the US, a response to the Panic of 1907 and repeated bank runs.
The 1910s, one event per year.Franz Ferdinand shot: Gavrilo Princip's shot in Sarajevo started the chain of alliances that pulled Europe into World War I.
The 1910s, one event per year.Lusitania sunk: It was sunk by a German U-boat, killing nearly 1,200 people, including many Americans, which angered the US.
The 1910s, one event per year.Easter Rising: Irish republicans seized the Dublin GPO, and the execution of their leaders shifted public opinion towards independence.
The 1910s, one event per year.Russian Revolution: There were two revolutions that year, and the Bolsheviks under Lenin seized power in October.
The 1910s, one event per year.WWI armistice: It was signed in a railway carriage at Compiegne, effective at the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month.
The 1910s, one event per year.Treaty of Versailles: It was signed in the Hall of Mirrors five years to the day after Franz Ferdinand was killed.

Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Safety pin: Walter Hunt reportedly twisted a piece of wire into this design to pay off a 15 dollar debt, then sold the patent for 400 dollars.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Snap fastener: Also called a press stud, it grips with a tiny ball-and-socket joint. It became a staple of baby clothes and Western shirts.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Zipper: Gideon Sundback made the design practical in 1913, but the name 'zipper' came later, from B.F. Goodrich's boots in the 1920s.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Masking tape: Richard Drew of 3M invented it for car painters, who were tired of ripping off paint along with their sticky tape.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Scotch cellophane tape: Drew's clear tape took its 'Scotch' name from a painter who complained the early version was stingy with its adhesive.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Duct tape: Developed for the US military to seal ammunition cases against water, it was first made from cotton duck fabric, hence 'duck tape'.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Velcro: Georges de Mestral invented it after studying burrs stuck to his dog's fur. The name blends the French 'velours' and 'crochet'.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Super Glue goes on sale: Harry Coover first stumbled on this cyanoacrylate while hunting for clear gun-sight plastic in the 1940s, and found it ruinously sticky.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Pritt glue stick: Henkel's inventor reportedly took the idea from a twist-up lipstick. It was the world's first glue stick.
Ways to hold things together, oldest to.Post-it Note: Spencer Silver's weak glue seemed a failure until colleague Art Fry used it to stop his hymnal bookmarks falling out.

Scottish inventions and discoveries.Logarithms (Napier): John Napier's invention turned multiplication into addition, powering slide rules for centuries. He also helped popularize the decimal point.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Watt's steam condenser: James Watt's separate condenser stopped engines wasting heat. The unit of power, the watt, is named after him.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Kaleidoscope (Brewster): Physicist David Brewster named it from Greek words meaning 'beautiful form seen'. It sold hundreds of thousands within months.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Waterproof raincoat: Charles Macintosh sandwiched rubber between layers of cloth. His name gave Britain the word 'mac' for a raincoat.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Telephone (Bell): Alexander Graham Bell was born in Edinburgh. His first successful call was the words 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.'
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Pneumatic tyre (Dunlop): John Boyd Dunlop, a vet, first made air-filled tyres to give his young son's tricycle a smoother ride.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Television (Baird): John Logie Baird's early sets used a spinning disc, and his first test image was a ventriloquist's dummy nicknamed Stooky Bill.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Penicillin (Fleming): Alexander Fleming noticed a mold killing bacteria in a forgotten dish. Florey and Chain later turned it into a mass-produced drug.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Radar (Watson-Watt): Robert Watson-Watt's work led to the Chain Home radar stations, which gave Britain early warning of aircraft in the Battle of Britain.
Scottish inventions and discoveries.Dolly the sheep: Born at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh, she was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, and was named after Dolly Parton.

Rovers and helicopters by mass.Ingenuity helicopter: It made the first powered flight on another planet in 2021, carrying a scrap of fabric from the Wright brothers' plane. It flew 72 times.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Sojourner: About the size of a microwave oven, it landed on Mars in 1997 and worked far longer than the planned week.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Pragyan: India's lunar rover rode in on Chandrayaan-3 in 2023, and its name means 'wisdom' in Sanskrit.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Yutu: Named Jade Rabbit after a Chinese myth, it stopped moving after two lunar nights, yet kept sending data for a lot longer.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Spirit: Built for a 90-day mission in 2004, it kept going for six years before it became stuck in soft sand.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle: It was the only vehicle in this list with seats. Folded flat, it was carried to the Moon on the side of the lander.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Zhurong: Named for a god of fire in Chinese mythology, it explored Mars from 2021, then went into hibernation and never woke up.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Lunokhod 1: Soviet drivers steered it from Earth in 1970, and it was the first remote-controlled rover on another world.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Curiosity: This car-sized rover landed in Gale crater in 2012, powered by a nuclear generator and equipped with a rock-zapping laser.
Rovers and helicopters by mass.Perseverance: It's gathering rock samples in sealed tubes, intended to be brought back to Earth, and it carried the Ingenuity helicopter to Mars.

Theaters and venues, by opening year.Theatre of Epidaurus: Its acoustics are so good that a dropped coin can be heard from the top row, and it seated about 14,000.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.The Globe (original): Shakespeare's company built it, and it burned down in 1613 when a cannon fired during a play set the thatch alight.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Comédie-Française: The world's oldest active national theater, it is nicknamed the House of Molière.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Covent Garden theatre: Today's building is the third on the site, which now houses the Royal Opera House, since earlier ones burned.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.La Scala: The Milan opera house premiered works by Verdi and Puccini, including Puccini's Turandot.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Palais Garnier: It inspired the setting of The Phantom of the Opera, and the real building does have an underground lake.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Moulin Rouge: Its red windmill sits atop the Paris cabaret that made the can-can a world-famous spectacle.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Carnegie Hall: Andrew Carnegie funded it, and Tchaikovsky conducted during its opening week.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Radio City Music Hall: This Art Deco gem in Rockefeller Center is home to the Rockettes and seats about 6,000.
Theaters and venues, by opening year.Sydney Opera House: Jørn Utzon's sail-shaped design won a competition, but he quit in 1966 after disputes and never saw it finished.

Distance from Tokyo.Seoul: The two cities are linked by the Haneda to Gimpo flights, reopened in 2003 as a shuttle between city airports.
Distance from Tokyo.Beijing: Beijing has been China's capital for most of the past 700 years, and it has the Forbidden City at its heart.
Distance from Tokyo.Hong Kong: Hong Kong returned from British to Chinese rule in 1997.
Distance from Tokyo.Bangkok: Its official ceremonial name is among the world's longest place names, and Thais usually call it Krung Thep.
Distance from Tokyo.Singapore: Singapore is both a city and a country, and one of the smallest in the world.
Distance from Tokyo.Honolulu: Japanese immigrants first arrived to work Hawaii's sugar plantations in the 1860s.
Distance from Tokyo.Sydney: Sydney is in the southern hemisphere, so Tokyo's winter is its summer.
Distance from Tokyo.London: In winter, Tokyo is nine hours ahead of London, so a morning meeting there is an evening one here.
Distance from Tokyo.New York: Tokyo is 13 or 14 hours ahead of New York, so a flight can arrive, in effect, before it left.
Distance from Tokyo.Rio de Janeiro: Brazil is home to the largest community of people of Japanese descent outside Japan.

Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Ruby-throated hummingbird: It beats its wings about 50 times a second and migrates across the Gulf of Mexico without stopping.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.House sparrow: Native to Eurasia, it was introduced to North America in the 1850s and is among the world's most widespread birds.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.American robin: Not related to the European robin, it was named by colonists who saw a resemblance.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Rock pigeon: They can find their way home and carried messages in wars; they descend from wild rock doves.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Barn owl: Its hearing is so sharp it can catch mice in total darkness, aided by a facial disc that funnels sound.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Herring gull: Chicks peck at a red spot on the parent's bill, a behavior famous from Tinbergen's studies.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Bald eagle: Its nest is the largest of any North American bird, and can weigh over a tonne.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Wandering albatross: It has the widest wingspan of any living bird, and glides for thousands of kilometres using the wind.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Pteranodon: It was a pterosaur, not a dinosaur, and had a long crest and no teeth.
Wingspans, from tiny fliers to flying gi.Quetzalcoatlus: This giraffe-height pterosaur was named for the feathered serpent god Quetzalcoatl.

When these handheld consoles launched.Game & Watch: Gunpei Yokoi created these single-game LCD gadgets, and its Donkey Kong version debuted the cross-shaped D-pad.
When these handheld consoles launched.Game Boy: Tetris came bundled with it, and its gray screen and long battery life beat flashier rivals.
When these handheld consoles launched.Virtual Boy: Its red-on-black 3D display flopped and it was dropped within about a year.
When these handheld consoles launched.Game Boy Color: Its color screen kept the line fresh, and Pokémon Gold and Silver arrived in this era.
When these handheld consoles launched.Game Boy Advance: Its wider screen and 32-bit chip played near-SNES games, and it still ran older Game Boy cartridges.
When these handheld consoles launched.Nintendo DS: Its name means Dual Screen, with a touch screen underneath, and it sold over 150 million units.
When these handheld consoles launched.Nintendo 3DS: It showed 3D images without glasses, though many players switched the effect off.
When these handheld consoles launched.Nintendo Switch: A hybrid that docks to a TV or goes handheld, it became one of Nintendo's best-selling machines.
When these handheld consoles launched.Steam Deck: Valve's handheld runs a Linux-based system and plays games from a Steam library.
When these handheld consoles launched.Nintendo Switch 2: The successor to the hybrid Switch, it plays most of its predecessor's games.

Milestones in psychology and the brain.Phineas Gage's accident: Phineas Gage survived an iron rod blasting through his skull, and his reported personality change became a landmark case for linking the frontal lobes to behavior.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Broca's area: Paul Broca found this region of the left frontal lobe by studying a patient who could only say 'tan', showing speech lives in specific brain areas.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Wundt's psychology lab: Wilhelm Wundt opened the first lab devoted to experimental psychology at Leipzig, which is why many date the field's birth as a science to this moment.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Freud's dream book: Freud's The Interpretation of Dreams sold poorly at first, yet it launched psychoanalysis; it was dated 1900 though released in late 1899.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Binet's intelligence test: Alfred Binet built this test to identify French schoolchildren needing extra help, not to rank people by fixed intelligence.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Rorschach inkblot test: Hermann Rorschach, a Swiss psychiatrist, published ten inkblots in his book Psychodiagnostik; he died the year after at just 37.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.First human EEG: Hans Berger recorded the first human brain waves in Germany, finding the rhythmic alpha waves that appear when we close our eyes.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.First lobotomy: Portuguese neurologist Egas Moniz developed the procedure and won a Nobel Prize in 1949, which is now widely seen as a deeply troubling honor.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Milgram obedience study: Stanley Milgram found about two-thirds of participants delivered what they believed were severe shocks when told to, shocking the public.
Milestones in psychology and the brain.Stanford prison experiment: Philip Zimbardo's study of mock guards and prisoners ended after six days instead of two weeks, and its methods and conclusions are now heavily criticized.

Reality competition premieres.Survivor (US): Based on Sweden's Expedition Robinson, the show's first winner was Richard Hatch, who later served a tax prison sentence.
Reality competition premieres.The Amazing Race: It won the first-ever Emmy for outstanding reality-competition program in 2003, and has won many more since.
Reality competition premieres.American Idol: The first winner was Kelly Clarkson, and the show was adapted from the British Pop Idol.
Reality competition premieres.Project Runway: Tim Gunn's 'Make it work' became the show's catchphrase, and Heidi Klum's 'One day you're in, the next day you're out'.
Reality competition premieres.Dancing with the Stars: The format comes from the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing, itself descended from Come Dancing, which began in 1949.
Reality competition premieres.America's Got Talent: Simon Cowell's variety contest named an 11-year-old singer, Bianca Ryan, as its first winner.
Reality competition premieres.RuPaul's Drag Race: RuPaul's contest turned drag into mainstream TV and has won many Emmys for outstanding reality-competition.
Reality competition premieres.The Great British Bake Off: The tent-based baking show moved from the BBC to Channel 4 in 2017, a split that made headlines.
Reality competition premieres.The Voice (US): The format is Dutch, and its famous spinning chairs mean coaches pick singers only by sound, not looks.
Reality competition premieres.Love Island (UK): The dating show had an earlier run in 2005, but its 2015 revival turned it into ITV2's biggest hit.

Steven Spielberg films by release.Jaws: A malfunctioning mechanical shark forced Spielberg to hide it, making it scarier. It is often called the first summer blockbuster.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Close Encounters: The aliens greet Earth with a five-note musical phrase composed by John Williams. Wyoming's Devils Tower is the star location.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Raiders of the Lost Ark: George Lucas's idea was inspired by 1930s serials. Harrison Ford's stomach bug in Cairo led to the famous shot-the-swordsman scene.
Steven Spielberg films by release.E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial: It briefly became the highest-grossing film ever. Sales of Reese's Pieces soared after the candy appeared on screen.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Hook: Robin Williams plays a grown-up Peter Pan who has forgotten who he is, with Dustin Hoffman as Captain Hook.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Jurassic Park: Its dinosaurs blended Stan Winston's animatronics with early CGI. The T. rex roar mixes animal sounds, including a baby elephant.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Saving Private Ryan: The 25-minute D-Day sequence at Omaha Beach is among cinema's most imitated openings.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Minority Report: Based on a Philip K. Dick story, with futurists consulted to design the 2054 technology, such as gesture-controlled screens.
Steven Spielberg films by release.Lincoln: Daniel Day-Lewis won his third Best Actor Oscar for playing the president.
Steven Spielberg films by release.The Fabelmans: A semi-autobiographical story of a young filmmaker growing up and his parents' split, drawn from Spielberg's own boyhood.

Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.あ a: The vowel row: a, i, u, e, o, which is why dictionary order starts here.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.か ka: Adding two small marks, the dakuten, turns か into が (ga).
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.さ sa: The 'shi' sound is irregular, because the original sound was 'si' before it shifted.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.た ta: Ta, chi, tsu, te, to: the pronunciation shifted over centuries, which is why 'chi' and 'tsu' break the pattern.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.な na: This is the only consonant row of the main five with no voiced or semi-voiced variants.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.は ha: As the topic particle, は is read 'wa', an old spelling quirk; with a small circle it becomes 'pa'.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.ま ma: After ya and ra, the final ん (n), though not in any row, sits at the end of the table.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.や ya: Only three kana here: ya, yu, yo; the gaps once held sounds that no longer exist.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.ら ra: Japanese 'r' falls between English r, l and d, which makes it tricky for learners.
Japanese kana rows, in dictionary (gojūo.わ wa: It once held wi, we and wo, and now only を (wo) survives, marking the object of a verb.

Making popcorn on the stove.Heat oil in a big pan: Popcorn needs oil that tolerates high heat, so coconut and canola are popular, since kernels only pop at about 180 degrees Celsius.
Making popcorn on the stove.Drop in three test kernels: Kernels pop at roughly 180 degrees Celsius, so three that pop quickly tell you the oil is hot enough for the whole batch.
Making popcorn on the stove.Wait for them to pop: Each pop happens when steam pressure inside the kernel finally ruptures its hull, turning the starchy centre into a white foam.
Making popcorn on the stove.Pour in the rest: The kernels that never pop are nicknamed old maids; they often have too little moisture or a cracked hull that lets steam escape.
Making popcorn on the stove.Put the lid on: Cracking the lid slightly lets steam out, which keeps popcorn crisp instead of chewy, while still stopping kernels from flying across the kitchen.
Making popcorn on the stove.Shake the pan: Shaking sends popped corn upward and moves unpopped kernels back to the hot base, helping every kernel get its turn and not scorch.
Making popcorn on the stove.Popping slows down: Once pops are more than a couple of seconds apart, pull the pan, because the remaining popcorn can burn quickly with no fresh kernels cooling it.
Making popcorn on the stove.Take off the heat: Popcorn is a variety of maize, Zea mays everta, with an unusually hard, moisture-sealing hull that other corn lacks, which is why only it pops.
Making popcorn on the stove.Tip into a bowl: Popcorn is a whole grain, and plain popped corn carries a good amount of fibre, far more than most snack foods.
Making popcorn on the stove.Toss with salt and butter: Melted butter makes salt stick, and fine salt clings better than coarse, which is why popcorn salt is ground extra fine.

Titanic (1997), in story order.Divers find a drawing: Titanic (1997) won 11 Academy Awards, tying the record set by Ben-Hur and later matched by The Return of the King.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Jack wins tickets at poker: The real wreck of the Titanic was found in 1985 by oceanographer Robert Ballard, about 3.8 kilometres down in the North Atlantic.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Jack stops Rose from jumping: Rose DeWitt Bukater and Jack Dawson are fictional, but many other characters, like Molly Brown, were real Titanic passengers.
Titanic (1997), in story order.\"I'm flying!\" at the bow: The famous bow scene was filmed on a huge, partly full-sized replica built in Rosarito, Mexico, in a custom seawater tank.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Jack draws Rose: The hands drawing Rose in the film are actually director James Cameron's own, and he sketched the artwork as well.
Titanic (1997), in story order.The car in the cargo hold: The car in the cargo hold was a Renault Type CB Coupe de Ville, and the real Titanic did carry one such Renault in its hold.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Titanic hits the iceberg: The real Titanic hit the iceberg at about 11:40 pm on April 14, 1912, and sank some two hours and forty minutes later.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Jack handcuffed below deck: Only about 700 of the more than 2,200 people aboard survived, and third-class passengers were far less likely to reach lifeboats.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Jack slips into the sea: The North Atlantic water was close to freezing, so those in it often survived only a matter of minutes.
Titanic (1997), in story order.Old Rose drops the necklace: The Heart of the Ocean is a fictional diamond, loosely inspired by real famous gems like the Hope Diamond.

Famous hoaxes and pranks.Cardiff Giant: A ten-foot petrified man was dug up on a New York farm; it was actually carved from gypsum by a tobacconist, George Hull.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Piltdown Man: This supposed missing link fooled experts for 40 years before 1953 revealed it was a human skull with an orangutan jaw.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Cottingley Fairies: Two girls photographed fairies, and Arthur Conan Doyle, creator of Sherlock Holmes, believed them; they confessed in the 1980s.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.War of the Worlds broadcast: Orson Welles's radio drama panicked some listeners, though later research suggests newspapers exaggerated the panic.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.BBC spaghetti harvest: The BBC's Panorama showed Swiss farmers harvesting spaghetti from trees, and viewers phoned asking how to grow their own.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Sidd Finch hoax: George Plimpton's Sports Illustrated article described a Buddhist monk with a 168 mph fastball, and readers believed it.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Taco Liberty Bell: Taco Bell ran a full-page ad claiming it had bought Philadelphia's Liberty Bell, and thousands of people called to complain.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Left-handed Whopper: Burger King claimed the sandwich had its condiments rotated 180 degrees, and customers really asked for it.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Gmail beta: Google announced it on April 1 with a gigabyte of storage, and many people thought it was a joke.
Famous hoaxes and pranks.Google Nose: This April Fools' joke let you search for smells, with a video of a supposed scent database.

Romantic movies, by release year.Casablanca: Its script was reportedly being written during filming, yet it won Best Picture and gave us 'Here's looking at you, kid.'
Romantic movies, by release year.Roman Holiday: Audrey Hepburn won an Oscar for her first major role, playing a runaway princess, and the film was shot on location in Rome.
Romantic movies, by release year.West Side Story: This musical retelling of Romeo and Juliet in 1950s New York won ten Oscars, a record for a musical at the time.
Romantic movies, by release year.Love Story: Its line 'Love means never having to say you're sorry' became one of the most quoted, and mocked, movie lines of the 1970s.
Romantic movies, by release year.The Princess Bride: Based on William Goldman's novel, it flopped at first, then became a cult classic quoted endlessly: 'Inconceivable!'
Romantic movies, by release year.When Harry Met Sally: The famous deli scene was partly improvised, and the line 'I'll have what she's having' was reportedly suggested by Billy Crystal.
Romantic movies, by release year.Titanic: It was the first film to earn over a billion dollars at the box office and tied the record with eleven Oscars.
Romantic movies, by release year.Notting Hill: The bookshop in the film was a real travel bookshop in west London, and the famous blue door has since been painted over.
Romantic movies, by release year.The Notebook: Based on Nicholas Sparks's debut novel, the film drew a devoted following mostly through TV and home video rather than its modest cinema run.
Romantic movies, by release year.La La Land: At 32, Damien Chazelle became the youngest ever Best Director winner, and its Best Picture mix-up at the Oscars is legendary.

DNA and genetics milestones.Mendel's pea paper: The Moravian monk's experiments with pea plants revealed the basic laws of heredity, but his work was ignored until around 1900.
DNA and genetics milestones.Miescher finds nuclein: Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher isolated this phosphorus-rich substance from white blood cells in pus-soaked bandages, discovering DNA.
DNA and genetics milestones.Avery shows DNA carries genes: Oswald Avery's team showed DNA, not protein, was the genetic material, though many scientists took years to accept it.
DNA and genetics milestones.Franklin's Photo 51: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray image of DNA's pattern was key evidence for the double helix, and was shown to Watson without her knowledge.
DNA and genetics milestones.Watson and Crick's helix: Their model, published in Nature, was just one page long, and the pair later shared a Nobel Prize with Maurice Wilkins.
DNA and genetics milestones.Sanger sequencing: Frederick Sanger's chain-termination method let scientists read DNA letters, and it earned him a second Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
DNA and genetics milestones.PCR invented: Kary Mullis's technique copies tiny DNA samples into billions of copies and became vital in forensics and virus testing.
DNA and genetics milestones.Dolly the sheep: Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born in Scotland, and she lived for about six years.
DNA and genetics milestones.Human Genome completed: The project mapped about three billion DNA letters and finished two years early, after more than a decade of international work.
DNA and genetics milestones.CRISPR gene editing: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier adapted a bacterial defense system into a precise editing tool and won a Nobel Prize in 2020.

Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Rashi: This French rabbi's commentary on the Bible and Talmud is so widely studied that it's printed beside the text in most editions.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Baruch Spinoza: Excommunicated by Amsterdam's Jewish community, the philosopher earned his living grinding lenses while writing the Ethics.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Moses Mendelssohn: This German philosopher championed Jewish emancipation and translated the Torah into German, helping Jews enter wider European culture.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Heinrich Heine: The German poet's verses were set to music by Schubert and Schumann, and his Lorelei poem is still sung.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Sigmund Freud: The founder of psychoanalysis, born in what is now the Czech Republic, fled Nazi-occupied Vienna for London in 1938.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Albert Einstein: In 1952 he was offered Israel's presidency, and he declined, saying he lacked the aptitude for dealing with people.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Franz Kafka: The Prague writer asked a friend to burn his manuscripts after his death, but the friend refused, saving The Trial and The Castle.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Anne Frank: The diary she kept while hiding in Amsterdam from the Nazis became one of the most widely read books of the 20th century.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Bob Dylan: Born Robert Zimmerman in Minnesota, he won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016 for new poetic expressions in song.
Famous Jewish figures, by birth year.Steven Spielberg: He directed Jaws, E.T. and Schindler's List, and founded the Shoah Foundation to record testimonies from Holocaust survivors.

Irish bands, by when they formed.The Chieftains: This traditional group, led by uilleann piper Paddy Moloney, won multiple Grammys and played with artists from Van Morrison to the Rolling Stones.
Irish bands, by when they formed.Them: Belfast band fronted by a young Van Morrison, they wrote 'Gloria', which became a garage rock standard.
Irish bands, by when they formed.Thin Lizzy: Led by Phil Lynott, they are best known for 'The Boys Are Back in Town' and twin lead guitars that influenced heavy metal.
Irish bands, by when they formed.Clannad: A family band from Donegal who blended folk with atmospheric pop, they included a young Enya before her solo career.
Irish bands, by when they formed.U2: Formed when Larry Mullen posted a notice at his Dublin school, the group has sold well over a hundred million records.
Irish bands, by when they formed.Hothouse Flowers: The Dublin band's soulful rock blended Irish roots, and they were discovered busking in the streets before their breakout hit.
Irish bands, by when they formed.The Cranberries: The Limerick band's 'Zombie' was a protest against violence in Northern Ireland, fronted by the late Dolores O'Riordan.
Irish bands, by when they formed.Boyzone: Put together by manager Louis Walsh, this Dublin boy band had many UK number ones and starred Ronan Keating.
Irish bands, by when they formed.Westlife: Formed in Sligo, the group scored 14 UK number-one singles, matching a record for the most by a group.
This Dublin post-punk band's name is a nod to a character in The Godfather, and their song lyrics are steeped in Irish poetry.
